initial_plan.can_answer_question: partly: the file has no distance-travelled or exposure measure, so it cannot estimate deaths per mile; it can show the annual total of recorded motorist deaths
initial_plan.metric: annual total number_of_motorist_killed recorded in police-reported crashes
initial_plan.population: motorist deaths recorded on police-reported NYC crash rows with crash_date in calendar years 2013 through 2025

data_check.rows: 2,132,218 crash rows in 2013–2025; annual row counts are in check_1.csv
data_check.missing_or_invalid: Among rows in the selected years, crash_date is missing/default/invalid in 0 rows and number_of_motorist_killed is missing in 0 rows.
data_check.coverage: All years 2013–2025 have records from January 1 through December 31; no partial year was found.
data_check.implication_and_decision: No selected rows need to be excluded or handled as a separate group for missing dates or motorist-death values. Use all dated crash rows and disclose that the file contains police-reported crashes only. The lower number of crash rows in later years does not change the count metric's definition, but this is not an exposure-adjusted risk measure.

final_plan.can_answer_question: partly: the data cannot answer whether deaths per mile declined because it contains no miles-driven denominator; it can describe annual recorded motorist-death counts
final_plan.metric: sum of number_of_motorist_killed per crash_date calendar year
final_plan.population: all police-reported NYC crash rows dated within each full calendar year 2013–2025, with recorded motorist deaths summed
final_plan.years: 2013–2025 inclusive; each year has records for all dates from January 1 to December 31
final_plan.limitations: No miles-driven exposure is present, so counts cannot establish per-mile risk. The data contains police-reported crashes only. No selected crash date or motorist-death value is missing, and no year is partial; all selected rows are retained.
